events.title: Artist Round Up: Collaging, Flyer Making, and the Community Zine
events.address: 101 W Vermilion St, Lafayette, LA
events.desc: AcA's Artist Roundups gather together artists and creatives for a casual night of making connections while also making art. By bringing artists of various backgrounds together, Artist Roundups hope to encourage dialogue and collaboration across artistic disciplines and create a shared sense of community and belonging. This month, join former Artist Alliance member Jesse Poimboeuf for a night of collaging and mixed media artmaking as we put together the 7th issue of the Creative Acadiana Community Art Zine. Inspired by the grassroots flyers handmade by the Artist Alliance in the 90s you'll collage flyers of your own: for real events, fake events, concepts, or anything else you can imagine! Collaging materials will be provided but you're also encouraged to bring your own. Old photos, stickers, interestingly patterned paper. Everything 2 dimensional is fair game. Scissors will be provided but if you may also bring other cutting utensils if you wish. Creatives of all levels welcome!

events.title: Twenty Years of Valcour Records
events.venue: Acadiana Center for the Arts - James Devin Moncus Theater
events.address: 101 W. Vermilion Street
events.desc: This show has sold out, but you can still watch the concert online! Join our waitlist to be notified if any seats open up prior to the concert. For two decades, Valcour Records has stood at the heart of Louisiana’s roots renaissance — preserving the traditions of Cajun, Creole, zydeco, and folk while amplifying the voices shaping its future. Founded in Eunice, Louisiana, by partners Joel Savoy and Phillip LaFargue, Valcour has become a touchstone for the state’s cultural identity, producing award-winning albums and nurturing artists whose music carries the sound and soul of Acadiana to audiences around the world. This special Louisiana Crossroads concert brings together the label’s musicians and collaborators for an evening that honors Valcour’s 20-year journey. Through live collaborations and stories, this evening traces the label’s evolution from a group of friends recording in Savoy’s living room, to a nationally respected imprint.   C.J. events.title: Southern Screen Film Festival with live Music by Sabine Mcalla
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
It’s night two of the Southern Screen Festival, and we’re celebrating with live music by Sabine McCalla ! A New Orleans favorite, McCalla brings soulful songwriting and a vibrant blend of American roots music, from Southern blues and soul to Brazilian samba. Her debut album, Don’t Call Me Baby , captures the sound that has delighted dancers and revelers for years. Join filmmakers, artists, friends, and fellow music lovers for good company and soulful sounds. sabine-mccalla.com

 

About the Artist

Sabine McCalla is a New Orleans singer-songwriter whose music brings together Southern soul, blues, Brazilian samba, and a broad range of roots influences. Her debut full-length album, Don’t Call Me Baby , released in November 2025 and co-produced by Ajaï Combelic and Sam Doores of the Deslondes, has earned more than 1.75 million streams and praise from publications including No Depression, Songlines, and Uncut. She has shared stages with Nick Shoulders, Rainbow Girls, John Craigie, and the Deslondes, and performed at the UK’s End of the Road Festival. Her work also extends to film, with an appearance alongside her sister Leyla McCalla in Ryan Coogler’s Sinners and performance and music contributions to Taylor McFadden’s Lovers . sabine-mccalla.com

Every week, the Lafayette Farmers and Artisans Market transforms the heart of Moncus Park into a lively gathering place, where local farmers, artisans, and craftspeople come together to share the best of our region. Wander the rows and you will find tables overflowing with just-picked produce, local honey, fresh flowers, baked goods, handmade crafts, and one-of-a-kind finds from the makers who pour their hearts into them. Whether you come for the produce, the people, or simply the joy of a morning outdoors, the market is where Lafayette starts its weekend. Come hungry, shop local, and make a morning of it! events.title: An Afternoon with Carrie Simon!
events.desc: Carrie will discuss her latest book, The Girl Who Ate Flowers, in a moderated Q&A led by Rachel Comeaux Lanclos. The Girl Who Ate Flowers is a story of the quiet town of Harvey, Louisiana, when it was shattered by the disappearance and murder of twelve-year-old Susanne Lee. Years later, the case remains unsolved when an unrelenting investigative journalist from The Manhattan Times, arrives determined to uncover the truth. But in Harvey, asking questions can be dangerous-and those who dig too deep don't always make it out. Haunting, atmospheric, and impossible to put down, *The Girl Who Ate Flowers* is a psychological thriller that grips readers to the final page-and just as the truth begins to surface, a shocking revelation suggests that Susanne's death is only the beginning.

events.title: Horace Trahan
events.desc:
Horace Trahan, the maker of the hit single, “That Butt Thing,” in 1999, is a world renowned Cajun and Zydeco artist, respected for his ability to pull the hell out of an accordion and belt out vocals that will give you chills. Having over-stepped boundaries and bypassed the stereotypes of naysayers, this native of Ossun, Louisiana, has made a huge and highly anticipated comeback on the music scene!
At the age of fifteen, Horace wanted to learn to play the accordion. His father brought him to Felix Richard, a strong accordionist and first cousin who lived in Cankton, LA. Horace was a natural and booked his first gig within six months of learning to play.
Horace was very comfortable in a musical setting, as he had purchased his first guitar at the age of twelve and had also begun playing the saxophone in the fifth grade. It was when he combined his angelic-pitched voice with the skills he honed on a Crown single row accordion, which the musical magic began. Horace was sixteen years old when he began singing Cajun music in French and in English. Not long after making his mark on bass drum in the marching band at Carencro High School and graduating, Horace hit the road and began touring with D.L. Menard. The road schedules would take the talented eighteen year-old musician to New York, Boston, Chicago, Canada, France, California, and the summer Olympics in Atlanta.
Two years later, in 1996, Horace and D.L. Menard recorded a CD on Swallow Records. During this time, at the age of…

events.title: Michael Juan Nunez and the Blue Orchestra
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Michael Juan Nunez is a Louisiana-born blues guitarist and vocalist whose music is deeply rooted in the rich musical traditions of his home state. Growing up in Lafayette, Nunez was surrounded by the sounds of Cajun, Zydeco, rock, and country music, which he absorbed from his parents and the vibrant local scene. As a child, he spent countless nights listening to the rhythmic pulse of Cajun and Creole music, experiences that would later shape his distinctive style.

Nunez’s career developed as he immersed himself in the blues, blending southern rock and roots influences with the soulful storytelling characteristic of Louisiana music. His performances are marked by heartfelt vocals and powerful guitar work, resonating with audiences through a fusion of deep southern blues, rock, and roots music. Over the years, he has become known for his energetic live shows and his ability to weave together traditional and contemporary sounds, earning recognition as a powerhouse in the Louisiana blues scene.

Nunez’s legacy lies in his commitment to preserving and evolving the musical heritage of Louisiana. By drawing from the region’s diverse genres and infusing his own creative spirit, he has contributed to the ongoing evolution of blues and southern rock, inspiring both audiences and fellow musicians with his authentic approach and passionate performances.

Hailing from Lafayette, Louisiana, and rooted deep in Cajun culture, Troy Richard serves up his own unique blend of musical gumbo. Bringing together a rich mix of sounds, influences, and Louisiana flavor, Troy delivers a solo performance that is as authentic and soulful as the roots he comes from.

Best known as a member of The Richard Revue, Troy steps out on his own to showcase his musical versatility and personality in a more intimate setting. With a sound steeped in South Louisiana tradition and a style all his own, he brings a little something for everyone.

From the heart of Acadiana to the stage, Troy Richard brings the flavor, the soul, and the spirit of Louisiana to every performance. Come hungry for some good music and get ready for a musical gumbo like no other!

events.title: Roddie Romero and The Hub City Allstars
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Straight out of the heart of Acadiana, Roddie Romero & The Hub City Allstars bring the unmistakable sound and spirit of South Louisiana to the stage. Blending traditional Cajun and Creole music with zydeco, swamp pop, blues, funk, soul, and rock 'n' roll, this powerhouse Louisiana band delivers a sound that is as deeply rooted as it is refreshingly original.

Led by singer, songwriter, accordionist, and slide guitarist Roddie Romero, the band celebrates the rich musical heritage of Louisiana while pushing its boundaries into exciting new territory. With soulful vocals, fiery accordion, masterful guitar work, and infectious rhythms, their music captures everything that makes South Louisiana special.

A three-time Grammy-nominated group, the Hub City Allstars have spent more than two decades performing at prestigious festivals and venues, earning recognition for their musicianship, original songwriting, and electrifying live performances. Their critically acclaimed albums, including The La Louisianne Sessions and Gulfstream , showcase a band equally comfortable honoring Louisiana's musical traditions and creating something entirely their own.

events.title: $ideQue$t
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
SideQuest LA

Two powerhouse Louisiana musicians, one shared love of great music. SideQuest LA brings together vocalist, songwriter, and drummer Gino V. and guitarist, vocalist, and songwriter Zach Edwards for a musical collaboration that refuses to stay in one lane.

Rooted in the sounds of South Louisiana but reaching well beyond its musical borders, SideQuest blends soul, blues, R&B, funk, hip-hop, and good old-fashioned rock and roll. The duo combines original songwriting with unexpected takes on some of their favorite songs, creating a show that is as versatile as it is entertaining.

Gino V., born and raised in Delcambre, Louisiana, is a seasoned musician known for his commanding vocals, deep grooves, and dynamic musicianship. He has performed with some of Acadiana's respected artists and notably played drums for Louisiana music legend Wayne Toups.

Zach Edwards adds his own distinctive guitar work, vocals, and songwriting to the mix, bringing together the blues, rock, and roots influences that make the SideQuest sound uniquely their own.

Whether delivering soulful originals, stretching out on a blues-rock groove, or putting their own spin on familiar favorites, SideQuest LA brings plenty of musical firepower and personality to the stage.

Expect big grooves, soulful vocals, killer guitar work, and a little bit of everything. SideQuest is anything but an ordinary night of live music.

events.desc:
Elise Riley

Carrying on a proud Louisiana musical legacy while bringing her own energy and personality to the stage, Elise Riley is part of a new generation keeping Cajun music alive and moving forward.

Born and raised in Lafayette, Louisiana, Elise grew up surrounded by the sounds and traditions of Cajun music. With legendary Louisiana musician Steve Riley as her father and musician Chris Stafford as her brother, music has always been a central part of her life.

A talented drummer, vocalist, and multi-instrumentalist, Elise has developed her own voice in the South Louisiana music scene. She co-leads Chère Élise, a Lafayette-based Cajun band that brings together traditional Cajun sounds and fresh musical influences. She also performs with Prends Courage, continuing to explore and celebrate the region's rich musical heritage.

Whether behind the drums or stepping forward as a vocalist, Elise brings infectious energy, musicianship, and a genuine appreciation for the music that shaped her.

Rooted in tradition but never afraid to make it her own, Elise Riley represents the next generation of Louisiana musicians carrying Cajun music into the future.

events.desc:
Grand Nathaniel

Hailing from Lafayette, Louisiana, Grand Nathaniel is the musical project of longtime Acadiana musician J. Burton, a fixture in the local music scene for more than three decades.

Blending dreamy lo-fi pop, synth-driven melodies, alternative rock, and nostalgic electronic textures, Grand Nathaniel creates music that feels both familiar and otherworldly. Drawing inspiration from decades of pop, rock, and experimental music, Burton crafts richly layered songs filled with atmosphere, imagination, and a little mystery.

A veteran of the Lafayette music scene, Burton has explored a wide range of sounds through projects including Dire Wood, FIGHTs, Talker, and Grand Nathaniel & the Ghosts. His solo work brings those musical experiences together in a distinctive style he describes as fantasy-pop.

With releases including At the Lagoon and Lonely Wanderer , Grand Nathaniel continues to build an imaginative musical world where nostalgic sounds meet fresh perspectives.

For fans of thoughtful songwriting, atmospheric pop, and adventurous indie music, Grand Nathaniel offers something a little different from the ordinary.

Come experience the sound and imagination of one of Lafayette's longtime independent musical voices.

events.title: Brass Bed
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Brass Bed

Emerging from Lafayette, Louisiana, Brass Bed has spent years carving out a distinctive place in the independent music scene with a sound that blends psychedelic rock, power pop, indie rock, and adventurous songwriting.

Formed in 2004, the band built a reputation for crafting catchy melodies wrapped in swirling guitars, analog synthesizers, fuzz, and expansive psychedelic textures. Drawing inspiration from artists like The Beatles, The Beach Boys, Big Star, and classic alternative rock, Brass Bed balances infectious pop sensibilities with an unpredictable, experimental edge.

The band earned critical acclaim with albums including Melt White (2010), The Secret Will Keep You (2013), and In the Yellow Leaf (2016). Their music has taken them beyond Louisiana, including a memorable appearance on NPR's Tiny Desk Concert series.

Featuring longtime members Jonny Campos, Peter DeHart, and Christiaan Mader, Brass Bed returned with new music in 2025, bringing fresh energy and sharper songwriting to their signature sound.

With deep roots in Acadiana and a sound that reaches far beyond regional boundaries, Brass Bed delivers a live experience full of shimmering melodies, gritty guitars, psychedelic exploration, and good old-fashioned rock and roll.

events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Some bands chase nostalgia. Dom Francis chases the feeling that made rock & roll matter in the first place.

Based in Austin, Texas, the band writes guitar-driven songs that blur the lines between rock, country, blues, soul, and Americana without ever sounding like a throwback act. Their music carries the grit of late-night bars, open highways, and dance halls—equal parts swagger and sincerity.

Onstage, Dom Francis favors momentum over spectacle. Their shows are loud, loose, and built to keep people moving, whether they're playing a neighborhood honky-tonk or a packed club. It's a live band in the truest sense: no gimmicks, no backing tracks, just musicians feeding off the room and each other.

As their audience continues to grow across Texas, Dom Francis is proving there's still a place for honest rock & roll—music that feels lived-in, timeless, and impossible to fake. After releasing his debut album “The Wanderer” in 2025, Francis presents us with his sophomore rock-leaning “The State of Things”

events.desc: The Grammy award winning Lost Bayou Ramblers’ evolution as a perversely progressive band rooted in Cajun traditions continues to excite, challenge, and redefine both genre expectations as well as cultural preconceptions. Founded in 1999 by brothers Andre and Louis Michot, the last 5 years have brought LBR a feature on Jack White’s American Epic, score contributions to the Oscar nominated film Beasts of the Southern Wild, a Grammy award for their latest album 'Kalenda' and tours with both Arcade Fire and the Violent Femmes. Lost Bayou Ramblers stands at the crosscurrents of Louisiana culture by inhabiting the gray area between Cajun and Creole, convention and innovation, mystery and a revelation, experimenting and growing the show to what it's become today: an eclectic mix of modern sounds and rhythms with ancient Cajun melodies and lyrics.  World Café says “The Grammy-winning group plays a revved-up version of Cajun music, shot through with punk energy and psychedelic fuzz.”

events.title: Artist Talk: Kate Gordon
events.address: 101 W Vermilion St, Lafayette, LA
events.desc: Join AcA Visual Arts Director Jaik Faulk in conversation with exhibiting artist Kate Gordon. Kate Gordon’s studio practice focuses on painting in the expanded field, sourcing inspiration from pop-up books, dioramas, and collage. The dream imagery that Gordon mines aims to capture the strangeness of the waking world, which is often not as logical as it might at first appear. Gordon has shown her paintings, collages, and video works nationally; exhibitions include a site-specific installation “Alligator Naps” at the Hilliard Art Museum, curation into the Weatherspoon Art Museum’s “Art on Paper” exhibition, and an invitation to create a public video installation at Block 2, a visual platform for new media artists in Raleigh, NC. Most recent professional accomplishments include participation in Kolaj Institute’s Artist Residency in Scotland, curation into “Is This Too Much?”, a maximalist exhibition at Le Mieux Galleries, and inclusion in the “Louisiana Contemporary” exhibition at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. Gordon currently holds the position of Associate Professor of Figure Drawing & Foundations at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette. She earned an M.F.A. from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and a B.F.A. from Pratt Institute.

events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
The Louisiana Surf Department is a swampadelic-country-rock band founded January 1, 2024 in Austin, Texas. On lead vocals and electric guitar, John Core of Crowley, Louisiana is truly the core of this music. He has carried most all of these songs for a long time on his journey to now – and has courageously brought this band together to help bring his songs to the world. Brian Bounds, hailing from north Texas, sits behind the drum kit and supports with backup vocals. Brian met John in Sedona, AZ in 2020.  After a chance reunion in Louisiana months later, their friendship was concretized in their first jam session. New-found little brother Markus “Shudawgy” Williams, originally from Tennessee, would not yet join the band, but first, invite a perfect stranger he saw on instagram into the fold. Enter James T. Carter, also from North Texas, on the bass guitar and backing vocals. James showed up to the house to jam, and the rest is history. James’ addition would solidify the trio, and January 1st, 2024 would mark their first organized rehearsal. After a year of digging into the project, Markus would reappear on the scene, this time with the intention of moving to Austin. “Young Man” as he is sometimes called, showed up, and kept showing up, and became a clear fourth member of the team. Not just for his world class guitar and musicality, but also for his world renowned hang. 

Mark your calendars! Louisiana Surf Department is rolling back into the Blue Moon Saloon on Friday…

events.title: Nether Hour
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc: Down in the heart of Austin, TX, where the music runs thicker than the heat, there's a band that's been making some serious noise. They call themselves Nether Hour , and they've been turning every dive bar and backroad juke joint into a full-blown musical revival. The band is a trio of unapologetic rebels, each one a powerhouse of sonic defiance. Bobby Flaco delivers gritty vocals and razor-sharp guitar riffs, while Bishop unleashes searing lead guitar and mandolin work, with Bercy laying down bass lines that slam right into your gut. Nether Hour is a relentless sonic melting pot, fusing the swampy grooves of Louisiana with Texas-sized doses of funk, blues, soul, and rock 'n' roll.

events.title: Mas Donkey
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Mas Donkey

Straight out of Lafayette, Louisiana, Mas Donkey brings a fresh dose of funk with a sound built for good times, deep grooves, and moving the dance floor. Blending funk, soul, rock, R&B, and a healthy dose of musical unpredictability, Mas Donkey delivers a style that is equal parts funky, playful, and undeniably original.

With a growing catalog of original music, Mas Donkey has developed a sound that moves effortlessly between infectious rhythms, soulful melodies, catchy hooks, and offbeat musical creativity. Tracks like 'Fresh Bowl of Funk,' 'GURL,' and 'Baby, Put Yo Phone Down' showcase an artist who isn't afraid to have fun, experiment with sounds, and keep listeners guessing.

Rooted in the musical spirit of Acadiana but drawing from a much wider world of funk and groove, Mas Donkey brings personality and originality to every performance.

If you like your music funky, your grooves deep, and your live shows full of surprises, Mas Donkey is ready to funkify your night!

events.title: Amis Du Teche
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.address: 215 East Convent Street, Lafayette, Louisiana, 70501, United States
events.desc:
Amis du Teche

Rooted in the rich musical traditions of South Louisiana, Amis du Teche celebrates the sounds, culture, and heritage of Acadiana through the timeless spirit of Cajun music. Drawing inspiration from the communities along the Teche, the band embraces the melodies, rhythms, and storytelling that have made Louisiana music such a treasured part of the region's identity.

With a love for traditional sounds and the lively spirit of a good Louisiana dancehall, Amis du Teche brings music made for two-stepping, waltzing, and gathering with friends. Their music honors the generations of musicians who came before them while keeping the Cajun tradition alive for new audiences.

Whether you're a lifelong Cajun music fan or simply looking for an authentic taste of South Louisiana, Amis du Teche brings the kind of music that makes you want to stay for one more dance.

Come celebrate the music, culture, and spirit of Acadiana with Amis du Teche!
